summary: ALGODEV-13 (S012 cross-sectional crypto momentum): extracted the shared cross-sectional layer (load_panels, rank_weights, portfolio_returns, metrics) from strategies/funding_carry.py into strategies/xsect_base.py; funding_carry now delegates with its public API unchanged (run_funding_carry.py output verified byte-identical, 45 S009 tests pass). Added strategies/xsect_momentum.py (XSectMomentumConfig, long winners / short losers, funding-aware accounting) and backtest/run_xsect_momentum.py. IS results (OOS >=2025-07-20 untouched): lb14 net Sharpe +0.92 at 0.055%/side taker, corr with S009 lb7 champion +0.009, 50/50 combo Sharpe 1.35 vs 1.02 S009 alone; Gate 0 no-look-ahead PASS. Caveat: per-year is NOT uniformly positive (lb14: 2021 -9.9%, 2025 IS-part -2.5%; lb30: 2025 -18.9%) — consistent with the ticket distrust of the preprint 2022-2024 window; Gate 1 walk-forward still required.

ALGODEV-13 Gate 1: refreshed Bybit data to 2026-08-30 and added backtest/wf_xsect_momentum.py (anchored walk-forward mirroring S009 E4). Standalone verdict: FAIL — stitched WF (2022..pre-OOS, net 0.055%/side) Sharpe +0.43, MaxDD -31%, 2022 -7.3% and 2025 -2.5% negative, all_years_positive=False. As a diversifier it still adds modest value: corr(WF S012, S009 champion)=+0.06; 25/75 combo Sharpe +0.84 vs +0.75 S009 alone with every year positive and MaxDD -18% vs -19%. Robustness grid is a plateau around lb14-30/n3 (no needle). Reserved OOS tail untouched.

ALGODEV-13: opened the reserved OOS tail (2025-07-20..2026-08-30, 407 days) with a single pre-declared final run (backtest/oos_xsect_momentum.py). Deployed config = anchored-WF choice on train only (lb14 n3, net 0.055%/side). OOS results: S012 alone Sharpe +1.19 / +40.7% total / MaxDD -12.6%; S009 champion +1.34; corr +0.093; combo 25/75 Sharpe +1.66, combo 50/50 +1.68 vs 1.34 S009 alone. Pre-declared decision metric (combo beats S009 alone on OOS) passed decisively — S012 confirmed as a diversifier for S009; standalone Gate 1 verdict (FAIL) stands.

ALGODEV-14 (meta-labeling over S007): applied the S004 meta-labeling methodology to S007 with three new scripts (backtest/s007_metalabel_data.py dataset builder, s007_metalabel_gate0.py no-look-ahead check, s007_metalabel_eval.py evaluation). Unit-of-learning decision: the DAY, not the individual add -- quantified on the engine's actual position lists (92% of traded days pyramid, 2233 adds, 79% share the first position's exit status via the common mid_range stop / day TP), so per-add labels would be pseudo-replicates; daily R aggregation preserved for passport comparability. Dataset: 680 traded days 2023-06-26..2026-08-11, 14 causal entry-time features (scenario/direction/height_bps/entry_minute/first_risk_frac/dist_to_tp_R/entry_pos_in_range/gap/asia range/prev-day ATR%/trend/dow), regression-verified (net +0.8008 R/day LIQFLOOR, +0.8665 NEWSSAFE at 0.635pt/side, byte-matching the 2026-08-21 passport numbers); Gate 0 PASSED (truncate at 2025-06-01, max|delta|=0 on all features). Evaluation: expanding yearly walk-forward (train<Y, test=Y, threshold chosen on train only), logit + small GBM, expectancy- and drawdown-targeted thresholds, on BOTH presets. VERDICT: FAIL -- every configuration skips days that are on average PROFITABLE (+0.66..+1.10 R/day skipped), total R always drops (LIQFLOOR logit/net +539.7R -> +435.0R stitched OOS), maxDD barely improves (-37.4 -> -36.7R) or worsens (NEWSSAFE logit/net -29.3 -> -42.1R); best DD-targeted cut (-37.4 -> -32.2R) costs -111R; worst day untouched (-8.87 -> -8.56R). The ticket's separate drawdown question is answered NO: the martingale-like DD comes from the intraday add path on chop days, which entry-time features do not predict. No engine/config change, no flag added; verdict recorded in s007_metalabel_eval.py docstring. Scripts left untracked like the S004 metalabel precedent.

ALGODEV-14 follow-up (worst-day tail study): found that ALL 30 worst days (<=-5R) on WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR are B 'double failures' (primary leg fully stopped, then the b_reversal_to_A recovery leg fully stopped too; 28/30 have exactly 8 positions). The pattern is NOT predictable: not by entry-time features (the meta-labeling FAIL), not at the flip moment (187 recovery legs, corr ~0 with flip time / realized damage / height), not by calendar (weekday flat, 0/30 on NFP or opex Fridays, 15:30-bar release proxy flat; the April-2024 cluster is one bad regime month), not by Asia/PDH-PDL liquidity geometry, and not by HTF context (counter-H1 days carry 2x tail rate at the SAME +0.75 expectancy). Two mechanical modifiers therefore tested via backtest/run_s007_tailrisk.py (pre-declared: cap=2, H1 SMA50, weight 0.5; Gate 0 on the H1 flag passed): (1) HTF half-risk on counter-H1 days REJECTED -- cuts profit more than drawdown (-18.5% sum for -15.3% maxDD), dominated by uniform size-scaling; (2) NEW ENGINE FLAG max_recovery_positions (default None = base untouched; regression: REF_PYRAMID_LIQ_DUKA + both working presets byte-identical with flag off) at cap=2 ACCEPTED for the prop worst-day axis only: -6.1..-6.7% profit for -25% worst day (-9.03 -> -6.75R), maxDD ~unchanged, all years positive on NEWSSAFE (2023 +24.6R) though 2023 dips to -0.8R on LIQFLOOR. Added preset WORKING_S007_PROP = WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE.with_(max_recovery_positions=2), explicitly NOT promoted to any bot config -- candidate pending Anton's decision; note it fixes only the DAILY-limit axis, not max total drawdown. Verdicts recorded in config.py flag comment and run_s007_tailrisk.py docstring.

ALGODEV-27 (S017 Elliott Wave rule-based, ZigZag+EMA200 on indices): implemented the full prototype -- frozen S017Config dataclass, non-repainting ATR-threshold ZigZag (pivots carry confirm_idx), impulse 1-2-3-4-5 rules, A-B-C correction rules, EMA200 trend filter, two entry modes (abc / wave4), event-driven R-accounted backtest with spread cost. Gate 0 PASSED (max|delta|=0 over 8 truncation points, M30+H1). Gate 1 FAILED: US500 anchored WF 2015-2025 stitched +3.5R/273 trades, 2/11 positive years (M30) and -22.3R, 3/11 (H1); NAS100/DAX cross-checks weak/negative with disagreeing best params (overfit signature). Strategy archived at prototype stage; OOS tail 2025-07..2026-06 reserved and never opened. Verdict baked into the module docstring.

ALGODEV-35: added liquidity_tp_ceiling_points (StrategyConfig) and wired it into engine.py::liquidity_tp -- caps a liquidity TP that lies beyond range_tp at range_tp+/-N points, on top of the existing liquidity_tp_floor (ALGODEV-21) which only stops a target being NEARER than range_tp. Prompted by a live 2026-09-02 case (Anton): a real S007 cycle picked liquidity 285.9pt beyond range_tp for its TP. Added 6 named presets (WORKING_S007_LIQCEIL10/20/30/40/50/100, all WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR + a ceiling) and backtest/run_s007_liqceiling.py sweeping all 6 against uncapped LIQFLOOR at Gate 1 (gross) and Gate 2 (real spread 0.635/side) on the same 2026-08-11 Dukascopy refresh run_s007_liqfloor.py used -- confirmed a byte-matching regression against that script before trusting the new numbers. Verdict: REJECTED, all six. Gate 2 net R/day for ceil10..100 = +0.676/+0.687/+0.729/+0.784/+0.833/+0.837 vs uncapped LIQFLOORs +0.801 -- every ceiling <=40pt is worse (lower net, often deeper maxDD, e.g. ceil20/30 -65R vs -50.9R) despite a higher day win-rate (61-63% vs 60%); ceil50/100 approach uncapped but do not beat it (ceil100s maxDD is identical to uncapped, i.e. the cap essentially never binds there). Conclusion baked into the preset comments: distant liquidity targets that look alarming on any single day are net CONTRIBUTORS to the 3+-year edge, not noise -- capping them tighter loses profitability. WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR (uncapped) stays the live preset; nothing promoted. default liquidity_tp_ceiling_points=None preserves byte-identical behavior for every existing preset (confirmed via the existing S007 test suite, 62 passed).

ALGODEV-43 (branch algodev-s007-breakeven-offset): added breakeven_offset_points modifier to S007. Default-off RAW-points field on StrategyConfig; when the breakeven rule fires the stop goes to entry+-offset (profit side) instead of exactly entry, so a retrace onto the BE stop clears the ~1.27pt spread+commission rather than booking it as a small loss. engine.py clamps offset to trigger-BE_OFFSET_MIN_GAP_POINTS; bot/s007_paper.py amend uses new pure helper breakeven_stop_price() (fill+-offset, clamped to the safe side of the latest M1 bar, floored at fill); plan_now surfaces it; run_s007_breakeven.py extended with a 0/1/2/3/5pt sweep + BE-exit breakdown. New preset WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05_OFF3 -- NOT promoted, NOT wired live. Sweep verdict: goal achieved (BE exits positive from ~2pt) but whole-book effect marginal/non-monotonic (MAX8_BE05 net R/day 0pt +1.6513 -> 3pt +1.6623 +0.7% -> 5pt +1.6217); clear maxDD gain (-19.2->-15.9R), clear worst-year cost (+173.9->+154.3R). Gate 3 not re-run. REF_* regression byte-identical. Not committed to master, not deployed. Left for Anton: pick offset, rerun Gate 3, decide on live repoint, sync Confluence/registry/passport.

ALGODEV-42 follow-up: added reversal_confirm_close (default False, base untouched) -- makes the b_reversal_to_A trigger require the same close-based two-bar confirmation setups.py::find_setup already uses for the primary A/B detection, instead of a bare intrabar low/high touch of mid. Motivated by a live 2026-09-16 incident (Anton spotted on the chart that a GER40 recovery leg armed off a single-tick wick touch of mid with no close confirmation -- verified against real broker bars). Backtested (run_s007_reversal_confirm.py, Dukascopy 2023-2026, real spread) against REVERSAL_S007/WORKING_S007/WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05 (live): confirm=True raises the recovery legs own win rate (53-67% -> 60-73%) and slightly improves the live presets maxDD/worst-year, but cuts net R/day by 2.9-4.1% on every base tested -- REJECTED on the expectancy axis, kept as a documented off-by-default flag. Verdict with exact numbers recorded in config.pys reversal_confirm_close comment; live preset unchanged (still confirm=False).

ALGODEV-44 follow-up, MAJOR finding: added exit_idx to every simulated position (purely additive, feeds no R/cost calc, byte-identical regression confirmed) and a new backtest (run_s007_execution_realism.py) that excludes ghost trades -- positions whose exit_idx-idx <= 1, i.e. entered AND resolved within 1-2 M1 bars, which a 1-minute-polling live bot can never execute regardless of code speed (bot/s007_paper.py::decide places a newly eod position the same cycle it is first detected, and that cycle is already >=1 bar behind real time by construction). Result: ghosts are ~24-30% of ALL positions across every preset tested (including plain BASELINE_S007, not just b_reversal_to_A/BE stacks) and account for 80-88% of each presets total positive R. Live preset WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05 collapses from the previously-quoted +1.6513R/day (maxDD -19.2R, all years positive) to a REALISTIC +0.22-0.30R/day (maxDD -77 to -96R, at least one realistically-losing year) once ghosts are excluded. Triggered by a live-vs-backtest parity check on 5 real trading days (2026-09-10/11/14/15/16) that found the model would have netted +.87 on the same real bars while live actually netted -.02 -- live is UNDERPERFORMING even the sobered-up realistic number, meaning the earlier-found whipsaw/entry-slippage issues are additional, real problems layered on top of this validation-methodology gap, not an alternative explanation for it. This calls into question every previously-quoted net-R/day number for every S007 preset (BASELINE_S007 through the live preset), since none of the prior validation excluded ghost trades. Not yet documented in Jira/Confluence or reflected in config.py preset comments -- pending Antons direction.

Built Gate 3 (prop-firm survivability) simulation for S021, requested by Anton same-day chat ("что бектестить, особенно с учетом пропа"), after the session-anchor question was resolved. Adapted the block-bootstrap Monte Carlo methodology from backtest/run_s007_propscheme.py (same thresholds: cashout +9%, daily limit -3%, total DD -10%; BLOCK_LEN=5, T_MAX=500, N_SIM=4000) to S021's much simpler at-most-1-trade/day structure: R = net_pts / (stop_adr_mult * ADR14) per trade, one R value per valid trading day (0.0 on no-trade days), full calendar day sequence preserved (not signal-days-only) so trade frequency stays realistic inside each 5-day block. Ran FILL_PROB=1.0 (no measured S021 execution-degradation figure exists, unlike S007's stated 3-of-4 heuristic -- fabricating one would misrepresent an unmeasured quantity) and instead stress-tested cost sensitivity directly (1.0bp baseline vs 3.0bp, matching the passport's own cost-sensitivity finding). Key results: longest historical losing streak = 8 (matches the passport's claimed 8-in-a-row exactly, independent confirmation); because S021 allows only 1 trade/day, the daily -3% limit is structurally almost unbreachable up to ~2.5%/trade risk (single-trade max loss ~= risk_pct), unlike S007 which pyramids intraday -- total drawdown, not the daily limit, is the binding constraint for S021. At 0.50-0.75%/trade: ~91-92% cashout rate, 2-8% total-DD bust, near-zero timeout -- the best risk band found on the grid tested (0.10/0.25/0.50/0.75/1.00/1.50/2.00%). Stress scenario (3bp cost) still gives ~80% cashout at the same risk band. Full grid results in reports/s021_propscheme_summary.csv.

ALGODEV-35: ran the existing-but-never-executed backtest/run_s007_liqceiling.py after a live 2026-09-22 incident (Anton spotted a TP at 25433.2 that turned out to be prev_day_low -- 95.8pt beyond range_tp, sourced from a single M1 wick, not a confirmed level). Result: capping liquidity_tp_ceiling_points tight enough to have actually constrained that case (10-40pt) costs net expectancy (+0.80R/day uncapped -> +0.68-0.78R/day) and does not improve maxDD -- REJECTED as a fix. Also committed the ALGODEV-42 reversal_confirm_close verdict from 2026-09-18, which had been tested and reported but never actually committed until now (backlog cleanup). Neither flag is enabled on any live preset. Discussed with Anton: the more promising direction, if revisited, is tightening what counts as a liquidity CANDIDATE (require confirmed structure) rather than capping distance after the fact -- not yet scoped or built.

Implemented S025 (US Index Overnight Drift, Confluence P12/S025+S026+S027 page 24838145): strategies/overnight_drift.py decomposes daily cash-to-cash return into overnight (open[t]/close[t-1]-1) and intraday legs with a gate0_no_look_ahead() regression check; 10 Gate 0 tests added in tests/strategies/test_overnight_drift.py (no-look-ahead, decomposition reconstructs exactly, cost strictly reduces equity). Found and handled a data-quality artifact while building backtest/run_overnight_drift.py: on data/raw/NASDAQ and data/raw/SP500 (composite-index proxies for the live NAS100/US500 CFDs), the 'open' column is backfilled equal to the prior close for most of older history (NASDAQ pre-2000-07-28, SP500 pre-2014-01-29 after fixing a first version of the detector that reported the wrong, too-early date by taking the first transient dip below threshold instead of the day after the LAST breach) -- added diagnose_open_data_quality() and made the runner clip to the detected clean window by default (--no-reliability-clip to disable). Honest E2 gross result on the clean window: overnight-only captures most of buy-and-hold's CAGR at much lower drawdown (SP500 2014-01-29..2026-08-14: overnight CAGR 7.46%/Sharpe 0.96/MaxDD -20.25%/WinRate 56.73%/12 of 13 years positive vs buy-and-hold CAGR 12.45%/Sharpe 0.76/MaxDD -33.92%; NASDAQ 2000-07-28..2026-08-14: overnight CAGR 7.80%/Sharpe 0.60/MaxDD -28.78% vs buy-and-hold CAGR 8.50%/Sharpe 0.44/MaxDD -80.37%). E3 cost sweep (0/1/2/3 bps round-trip per side, common 2014-01-29+ window) shows the edge is thin and cost-fragile: near breakeven around 1.5-2bps/side and clearly negative by 3bps on both indices -- consistent with the module's own factor-decay-after-publication caveat. No promotion decision made; still idea-stage per the registry/passport, now with a real (gross+costed) backtest attached instead of a formalized-rules-only spec.

Anton's request: benchmarked stop_mode="last_swing" (existing engine mode, never tested against the current live TP logic tp_mode="liquidity") against the live stop mid_range, on top of the exact live preset WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05_OFF2. Added a new default-off field last_swing_buffer_points (StrategyConfig) that pushes the last_swing stop N raw points further from entry (same idea as breakeven_offset_points), applied in pick_stop() only to the swing candidate (not the range_stop fallback); pick_stop signature gained a last_swing_buffer_points=0.0 kwarg, both call sites updated, both existing REF_PYRAMID_DUKA/REF_PYRAMID_LIQ_DUKA regression presets unaffected (0.0 default is a no-op by construction, 33 existing engine/bot tests pass unchanged). New backtest/run_s007_last_swing_stop.py sweeps buffer {0,1,2,3,5}pt at Gate 1 (gross) and Gate 2 (real spread 0.635/side), Dukascopy 2023-06-26..2026-08-11. VERDICT: REJECTED, decisively -- best last_swing variant (buf=1.0pt) nets +0.072R/day vs live mid_range's +1.629R/day (>95% expectancy loss), maxDD 8-9x worse (-136R vs -17R), 2023/2024 turn net-negative outright. last_swing stops MORE often than mid_range, not less (78-82% of positions vs 69.5%, +441..+641 more stopped): per-position stops right behind the last swing get tagged by ordinary pyramiding-leg pullbacks that mid_range's wide shared stop never sees. Closes the open item in strategy-spec-S007.md sec 4/13 (last_swing was the one individual-stop mode still in the engine but never benchmarked on tp_mode="liquidity"). Full verdict + numbers table written as a comment on last_swing_buffer_points in config.py, per strategy-modifiers convention. No preset added (nothing here is a deployment candidate); live preset (bot/s007_config.py::PRESET, webapp DB account_strategies.preset id=1) untouched.

Implemented S027 (Sector ETF Cross-Sectional Momentum, Confluence P12/S025+S026+S027 page 24838145): strategies/xsect_equity_momentum.py reuses strategies/xsect_base.py's rank_weights()/portfolio_returns() (same engine as live S009 / S012) on the 11 SPDR sector ETFs (XLE/XLF/XLK/XLV/XLI/XLY/XLP/XLU/XLB/XLRE/XLC) instead of crypto perps -- funding_day is a zero frame since ETFs pay no funding, xsect_base.py itself left untouched (backs the live S009 book). Default formation window 126/21 trading days (Jegadeesh-Titman-style 6-1 month, deliberately different from S012's 30/0 crypto default) -- a literature-motivated first guess, not tuned. Deliberately did NOT reuse xsect_base.metrics() (hardcodes 365 cal. days/yr for always-on crypto; would mis-annualize a ~252-day/yr equity book) -- used utils.report.make_report(periods_per_year=252) instead, same convention as fx_carry/overnight_drift. Fetched real data via utils.data.load_yf() (11 new data/raw/<TICKER>/<TICKER>_1d.csv caches, 2000-01-03..2026-09-21 for 9 sectors, XLRE from 2015-10-08, XLC from 2018-06-19 -- real SPDR launch dates). 7 Gate 0 tests added in tests/strategies/test_xsect_equity_momentum.py (no-look-ahead, zero-funding reduces to plain price return, dollar-neutral weights, min_universe floor flattens thin days); full tests/strategies/ suite (55 tests) green, no regression to S009/S012/xsect_combo. Gate 0 PASS on real data. Honest E2 gross result with the untuned default config, full 2000-01-03..2026-09-21 history: Sharpe 0.04, CAGR -0.00%, WinRate 51.0%, 13 of 27 years with a positive mean daily net return -- essentially NO edge, and E3 makes it worse (Sharpe -0.05 at 2bps/side, -0.19 at 5bps/side). No parameter search was run to try to find a positive result (would be exactly the overfitting this project's own conventions warn against, e.g. S001/S002/S016). Likely structural reason, stated as a hypothesis not a proven cause: 11 SPDR sectors are all slices of the same S&P 500 and highly intercorrelated, so cross-sectional return dispersion is much smaller than S012's ~24 more idiosyncratic crypto perps -- a fundamentally weaker setting for a rank-the-extremes momentum book. No promotion; registry status stays idea (now idea-with-a-null-first-backtest, like S001/S002/S016), not backtested with a live edge.

Corrected the S027 implementation after re-reading the actual Confluence spec (page 24838145, S027 heading says 'месячный ребаланс' + long-only top-N): the first draft (see preceding change-log entry, same session) had mechanically copied S012's daily dollar-neutral long/short book onto the new universe without checking it matched what S027 itself specifies. Rewrote run_backtest() to be the canonical spec'd version: monthly rebalance (decide on the last trading day of each month from that day's fully-realized signal via monthly_momentum_signal(), apply starting the NEXT trading day via one shift(1), hold flat until the following month -- own no-look-ahead convention, distinct from S012's same-day-shift convention since here the signal is not applied same-day), long-only equal-weight top-N (own weight builder, _long_only_top_n_weights_at() -- xsect_base.rank_weights() cannot produce a long-only book, it always divides by bottom_n). Kept the original daily dollar-neutral version, renamed run_backtest_dollar_neutral_daily_variant(), explicitly labeled as an exploratory variant, not 'the' S027 -- both still reuse xsect_base.portfolio_returns() (periodicity-agnostic, safe for both); xsect_base.py itself untouched throughout (backs the live S009 book). 11 Gate 0 tests now (was 7): added test_monthly_rebalance_dates_are_month_ends_only (weights must only change the day after a detected month-end) plus no-look-ahead/long-only/min-universe/cost coverage for the canonical path, kept the daily-variant's original tests renamed to match. Full tests/strategies/ suite (59 tests) green. Added an equal-weight-all-11-sectors (no ranking) benchmark to the runner -- this is the honest finding: the momentum-ranked top-3 book (CAGR 6.95%/Sharpe 0.46/MaxDD -47.08%, gross, full 2000-01-03..2026-09-21 history) is statistically indistinguishable from the naive equal-weight benchmark (CAGR 6.86%/Sharpe 0.46/MaxDD -53.92%) -- the momentum SELECTION adds no measurable value over plain diversified US sector beta with these untuned parameters; cost sensitivity is small either way since monthly rebalance means low turnover (Sharpe only drops 0.46->0.42 at 10bps/side). This agrees with the daily dollar-neutral variant's own honest null result (Sharpe 0.04) -- both readings say the same thing: 11 highly intercorrelated S&P 500 sub-indices give too little cross-sectional dispersion for rank-based selection to show an edge here. No parameter search was run to look for a positive result. No promotion; still idea stage with a null-to-negative first backtest under two different, both spec-consistent-ish, constructions.

Started S026 (WTI Crude Oil, EIA event volatility, Confluence P12/S025+S026+S027 page 24838145) with the piece the spec itself flags as the biggest non-statistical risk: the exact EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report release calendar (Wednesday 10:30am ET default, shifts around holidays). Fetched the live schedule (https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/schedule.php) and verified a general rule against all 14 published holiday-shift rows (2024-12..2026-11): if a US federal holiday (holidays package, US calendar) falls on the Mon/Tue/Wed of the normal release week, EIA delays Wed->Thu -- matches 13/14 rows exactly. The 14th (week ending 2025-12-19, released 2025-12-29 Monday, not a simple +1 day) is a genuinely irregular year-end production gap that is NOT rule-derivable -- kept as an explicit, dated KNOWN_HOLIDAY_SHIFTS override table (all 14 rows, source-linked, dated 2026-09-23 fetch) rather than guessed at. eia_release_datetime() checks the table first, falls back to the verified general rule, and RAISES UnregisteredYearEndShiftError (does not guess) for any future December/January week whose default Wednesday lands within 2 days of Christmas or New Year's Day and isn't yet registered -- confirmed this guard correctly flags all 14 such weeks 2015-2026 in the runner check below (12 pre-dating this table's coverage, 2 right at its edges). 23 tests in tests/strategies/test_eia_calendar.py (all 14 published rows individually, the general-rule-alone reproduction, the raise-not-guess behavior, ordinary weeks). Full tests/strategies+utils suite (100 tests) green. Then wrote backtest/run_eia_calendar_check.py -- NOT a backtest, a data-availability check -- which found the actual, hard blocker: yfinance only serves ~60-70 calendar days of intraday (15m/30m/1h) CL=F history (a Yahoo platform limit), vs. ~51 EIA events/year -- at most 8-9 usable historical events, far below even the spec's own already-flagged-as-thin ~50/year concern. No backtest was run or fabricated on this insufficient sample. Documented two real paths forward, neither attempted (both need Anton's explicit go-ahead): (1) cTrader Open API historical trendbars -- bot/ctrader_orb.py, ctrader_s007.py, ctrader_s011.py already use ProtoOAGetTrendbarsReq against the live demo account for other CFDs; if the broker has an oil CFD with deep minute history, same pattern, new symbol, but touches live broker credentials so not wired up here; (2) start a forward-only collector now (same irrecoverability logic as the Deribit options-snapshot job in infra-scheduled-jobs-spec.md), accepting a usable sample is a year+ away. S026 status: calendar infrastructure built and tested, backtest blocked on data, explicitly not faked.

Implemented S022 (Asia Mean Reversion, EUR/USD -- Bot 1 of Anton's three-bot brief, claude/strategies-registry.md S022, spec: VWAP+Z-Score, BUY Z<=-2.2 & RSI(14)<=30, SELL Z>=+2.2 & RSI(14)>=70, exit on VWAP touch or SL=1.5xATR(14)). Also wrote two new shared modules used by all three S022/S023/S024 bots: utils/histdata.py (load_histdata_m1_utc/resample_ohlc -- reads DAT_ASCII_<SYM>_M1_*.csv directly and converts histdata's fixed-EST-5 clock to true UTC, exact/unambiguous since the spec's session windows are all given in UTC, unlike strategies/orb_intraday's deliberate non-conversion for S021) and utils/indicators.py (wilder_rsi/wilder_atr, textbook SMA-seeded Wilder definitions, causal). Documented judgment calls (see module docstring): histdata's FX feed carries no real volume (verified always 0), so VWAP is approximated as the session-anchored cumulative average of typical price (H+L+C)/3, equal-weighted per M5 bar, not a genuine dollar-VWAP; entries execute at the bar AFTER the signal bar's open (not an idealized same-bar-close fill); stop-vs-VWAP same-bar ties resolve stop-first (conservative); at most one trade per session. RSI(14)/ATR(14) computed continuously across the whole M5 series, not reset per session. 9 Gate 0 tests (no-look-ahead via truncation at both session and intraday cutoffs, session-causal VWAP/Z reproduction by hand, next-bar-open entry timing, one-trade-per-session, ATR-at-signal-bar stop sizing, stop-before-VWAP tie-break) -- all pass.
